interface.name: wdm_greeter_v1

description.summary: login and session control for a wdm greeter

interface.description:
The singleton object a wdm greeter binds to log a user in.
The protocol has three phases. On bind the compositor pushes the enumerate phase: the available users, the available sessions, the rank of each output, and any error from a previous failed launch, terminated by "done". The authenticate phase mirrors PAM's conversation, since PAM asks an arbitrary number of questions in an arbitrary order. The launch phase is a single start_session request, after which the compositor tears the greeter down and hands the display to the user's session.
The compositor performs authentication itself; credentials never reach a process that can read the shadow database. The greeter is untrusted and rate limiting is enforced compositor-side.

entry.name: auth_in_progress
entry.summary: create_session while a conversation is already active

entry.name: no_auth
entry.summary: respond or start_session outside an authenticated state

entry.name: stale_prompt
entry.summary: respond carried an id that is not the pending prompt

entry.name: invalid_session
entry.summary: start_session named a session id that was never advertised

entry.name: invalid_env
entry.summary: the env array is not NUL-separated NAME=VALUE entries with NAME matching [A-Za-z0-9_]+

enum.name: session_type

description.summary: how a session expects to be displayed

enum.description: A wayland session is expected to acquire DRM master itself once the compositor has released it. An x11 session is expected to bring up its own X server; wdm never starts one.

enum.name: prompt_style

description.summary: how a prompt should be presented

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroying the object cancels any conversation in progress.

request.name: create_session
request.description:
Starts a PAM conversation for the named user. The compositor answers with a series of prompt events and finally auth_ok or auth_failed.
Raises auth_in_progress if a conversation is already active; call cancel first. The compositor rate limits repeated attempts and may delay a response, so a greeter must not assume a prompt arrives promptly.

arg.name: username
arg.summary: a user advertised by a user event

request.name: respond
request.description: The id must match the pending prompt or stale_prompt is raised; this keeps a slow greeter from answering a question that has been replaced.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: the id from the prompt event

request.name: cancel
request.description: Aborts the PAM conversation. No auth_ok or auth_failed follows. It is not an error to cancel when no conversation is active.

request.name: start_session

description.summary: launch a session for the authenticated user

request.description:
Valid only after auth_ok, otherwise no_auth is raised.
On success the compositor releases DRM master, disconnects the greeter, and executes the session. There is no reply: a successful launch ends this connection. If the launch fails the greeter is relaunched and told why through last_error.

arg.name: session_id
arg.summary: an id from a session event

arg.name: env
arg.summary: additional NUL-separated KEY=VALUE entries for the session

event.name: user
event.description: Sent during the enumerate phase for each user with a uid at or above UID_MIN whose shell is not a nologin shell.

arg.name: last_session
arg.summary: session id used at this user's last successful login, empty if none

event.name: session
event.description: Scanned from the wayland-sessions and xsessions directories under /usr/local/share and /usr/share, in that order — an entry in /usr/local/share shadows a distribution entry with the same id.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: stable identifier, the desktop file name

arg.name: exec
arg.summary: the command line to be executed

event.name: output_rank
event.description:
Rank 0 is the primary output. Ranks are contiguous from 0 across all currently connected outputs, ordered by the compositor's configuration.
Re-emitted whenever the set of connected outputs changes, so unplugging the primary output promotes another to rank 0 and the greeter is expected to move its login surface. Policy is the greeter's: it may draw only on rank 0, or draw on every output and place the login form on rank 0.

event.name: last_error

description.summary: report why the previous launch failed

event.description: Sent during the enumerate phase only when the greeter was relaunched after a failed session launch. Without this a user sees an unexplained bounce back to the login screen.

event.name: done
event.description: All initial user, session, output_rank and last_error events have been sent. output_rank may still be re-emitted later on hotplug.

event.name: prompt
event.description: Answer with respond carrying the same id. Only one prompt is pending at a time. Prompts with style info or error expect no response.

event.name: auth_failed
event.description: The conversation is over. create_session may be sent again, subject to rate limiting.
